record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Fix n and let T(n) be the parameter space of Euclidean n-gons up to scaling, λ the natural probability measure on T(n), and E(n) the set of ergodic n-gons. Is λ(E(n)) positive?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Fix an integer $n \geq 3$. Let $T(n)$ denote the parameter space of Euclidean $n$-gons considered up to similarity (i.e., up to scaling, translation, and rotation), parametrized for instance by the $(n-2)$ interior angles together with $(n-3)$ side-length ratios that determine a simple polygon shape. Equip $T(n)$ with the natural probability measure $\lambda$ induced by Lebesgue measure on this finite-dimensional parameter space. For each polygon $P \in T(n)$, consider the billiard flow inside $P$ on the unit tangent bundle, and call $P$ ergodic if this billiard flow is ergodic with respect to the natural Liouville measure. Let $E(n) \subset T(n)$ be the set of ergodic $n$-gons. Determine whether $\lambda(E(n)) > 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the set of ergodic $n$-gons has positive measure in the parameter space of $n$-gons is a long-standing open problem in polygonal billiard theory. Known results (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie) establish that for rational polygons the directional flow is uniquely ergodic in almost every direction, but rationals form a measure-zero subset of $T(n)$. No example of an irrational nonergodic polygon is known, and conversely no positive-measure set of ergodic polygons has been identified. Multiple recent surveys list this as open.

status_evidence.title: polygonal billiards: some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists ergodicity in polygons among standing open problems; no positive measure result known.
status_evidence.claim: The positive-measure ergodicity question for polygons is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: For rational polygons directional flows are uniquely ergodic in a.e. direction, but the question of full ergodicity for typical (irrational) polygons remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: No known result establishes positive measure of ergodic polygons.

status_evidence.title: Classical and Open Problems about Billiard Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes that ergodicity of typical polygonal billiards is unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: Status of ergodicity for typical polygons is open.
